name: B10-0315/2025 – Motion for a resolution (as a whole)
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the Commission delegated regulation of 10 June 2025 amending Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675 to add Algeria, Angola, Côte d’Ivoire, Kenya, Laos, Lebanon, Monaco, Namibia, Nepal and Venezuela to the list of high-risk third countries which have provided a written high-level political commitment to address the identified deficiencies and have developed an action plan with the FATF, and to remove Barbados, Gibraltar, Jamaica, Panama, the Philippines, Senegal, Uganda and the United Arab Emirates from that list
part_text:
The European Parliament is blocking a European Commission plan that would have removed the United Arab Emirates from the European Union's list of high-risk countries for money laundering and terrorist financing. The Parliament says the United Arab Emirates has made some improvements, but not enough. It wants the Commission to check the country more thoroughly first. The Parliament also criticises the Commission for grouping many countries into one act, which stops each country being judged on its own.

- The plan to remove the United Arab Emirates from the high-risk list is blocked for now.
- Banks and other firms must keep applying extra checks to customers linked to the United Arab Emirates.
- The Commission must propose a new plan that answers these concerns.
